property_summary: A fresh C accepts initialize(address) exactly once: the first call succeeds and any subsequent initialize call reverts with InvalidInitialization.
A C that has not been initialized rejects setSlopes with a revert for every input (access control is unset, so AccessDenied fires), even when the slope data itself is valid.
A C that has not been initialized rejects setLimits with a revert for every input (access control unset, so the checkAccess modifier denies the call), regardless of the limit values.
Once initialized with an access control contract that grants access, C accepts setSlopes with any valid slope data (0 < kink < 1e27), i.e. the call must not revert.

property_summary: setSlopes reverts exactly when the kink is 0 or >= 1e27 (given access is granted), and otherwise stores and emits the given slopes.
On a freshly deployed C (zero slopes, zero multiplier), rate() over a mock vault reverts exactly when the vault's utilization is 0, and otherwise returns an interest rate of 0.
On a fresh C, rate() reverts exactly when the vault's utilization is 0, and otherwise returns 0.
On a freshly deployed C, setSlopes reverts (AccessDenied) for any valid kink, since no caller has been granted access.
An unauthorized caller can never modify the slope data: c.setSlopes always reverts, for every asset and every slope/kink input.
c.setSlopes always reverts whenever the given slope data has kink == 0 or kink >= 1e27, regardless of other parameters.
An unauthorized caller can never change the limits: c.setLimits always reverts, for every maxMultiplier, minMultiplier and rate input.
c.rate always reverts when the given vault address has no deployed code, for every asset.
